findings.title: [P2] Retain truncated HTTP responses as transport failures
findings.body: A server closing a chunked response prematurely causes HTTPResponse.read1() to raise http.client.IncompleteRead, which derives from HTTPException and is not caught here. This behavior is confirmed by the [pinned CPython source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/v3.14.5/Lib/http/client.py). The exception reaches the outer incomplete-stop handler, abandoning subsequent fixed attempts. Handle this ordinary transport failure in paired.py by retaining an unknown slot and continuing the remaining requests without retrying; the immutable Fetcher and transport dependencies need no changes.

findings.title: [P2] Reconcile representation states after forced child termination
findings.body: If cancellation arrives during read1(), the transport masks SIGTERM and the child can exceed the parent's five-second grace period, causing SIGKILL before the worker changes its saved 'attempting' slot to 'interrupted'. Parent recovery updates the request ledger but checkpoints event_outcomes unchanged here. The final representation therefore remains 'attempting' after child exit, while its shadow-clock status can still say 'not_attempted'. Reconcile affected slots with the recovered ledger and rebuild event_result before saving the final incomplete summary.

overall_explanation: Ordinary truncated HTTP responses can prematurely abandon the fixed attempt sequence, and forced cancellation can leave inconsistent terminal representation states. These findings concern the new orchestration code, not compatibility changes to the immutable dependencies. Review used read-only inspection; no tests, acquisition, or private-data access were performed.
